META.subject: Core Mathematics
META.titleDoc: CORE MATHEMATICS GRADE 10: QUADRATIC EXPRESSIONS AND EQUATIONS
META.subtitleDoc: OpenAI-only evaluation • Sub-Strand 1.3 • 14 lessons • teacher review copy

UNIT.sep: Model area,derive identities and test algebraic and contextual solutions.
UNIT.careers: Illustrative mathematical modelling and paper design planning;no professional qualification or real construction claim.
UNIT.focus: Quadratic expression formation,area identities,numerical identities,factorisation,equation formation,solutions by factorisation and real-life paper models.
UNIT.content: Quadratic expressions; Quadratic identities; Factorisation of quadratic expressions; Formation of quadratic equations; Solution of quadratic equations by factorisation; Application of quadratic equations to real-life situations
UNIT.phenomenon: A fictional design chart drops a cross term,loses a zero root and accepts a negative width because it solves an equation.
UNIT.supportingPhenomena: Labelled area partitions,coefficient checks,zero products,repeated roots and changed-area model comparisons.
UNIT.drivingQuestion: How do we use equations in daily life?
UNIT.storylineThread: Expression→area sum→area differences→numerical use→common factor→monic→nonmonic→equation formation→zero-product→complete roots→context→exploration→audit→independent evidence.
UNIT.coreCompetencies:
Critical thinking and problem solving: the learner interprets statements to form and solve quadratic equations to get solutions to real-life cases.
Communication and collaboration: the learner discusses with peers and comes up with quadratic identities.
UNIT.values:
Unity: the learner works with others to write quadratic identities on a chart.
Respect: the learner works with peers to form and solve quadratic equations to get solutions to real-life cases.
UNIT.pcis: Socio-economic and environmental issues (social cohesion): the learner works with peers to form and solve quadratic equations to get solutions to real-life cases.
UNIT.subject: Core Mathematics
UNIT.learningOutcomes:
form quadratic expressions from different situations,
derive the quadratic identities from the concept of area,
apply quadratic identities in numerical cases,
factorise quadratic expressions from different situations,
form quadratic equations in different situations,
solve quadratic equations by factorisation,
apply quadratic equations to real life situations,
explore the use of quadratic equations in real life situations.

FINAL_EXPLANATION.instructions: Lesson14,40minutes:4procedure,8section1,8section2,8section3,10section4 and2independent checking. Work independently with CQE14,plain paper and ruler;no teaching cards,peers or worked keys. Use exact arithmetic,show derivations/factors and check roots in original equations. Paper models only.

sections.title: 1. Form an expression and derive an identity
sections.prompt: Using CQE14,form and expand the expression for the rectangle’s area. Independently draw and label the square of side p+q split at p on both adjacent sides. Label all four region areas and use them to derive (p+q)². Explain the positive-length condition of the drawing and the separate algebraic extension.
sections.exemplar: Rectangle area x(x+4)=x²+4x. Four labelled square regions have areas p²,pq,pq,q²,so(p+q)²=p²+2pq+q². The area diagram uses positive p,q;expanding(p+q)(p+q) separately establishes the identity for all real p,q. Both cross rectangles are required.

sections.title: 2. Use an identity and factor a quadratic
sections.prompt: Evaluate99² through an appropriate quadratic identity,showing every term. Factor2x²+5x−3 and verify by full expansion. Explain why matching only the constant term would be insufficient.
sections.exemplar: 99²=(100−1)²=10000−200+1=9801. 2x²+5x−3=(2x−1)(x+3),because expansion gives2x²+6x−x−3. The leading,middle and constant coefficients must all match;the constant alone does not establish an identity.

sections.title: 3. Form an equation and solve by factorisation
sections.prompt: Form one monic quadratic equation with roots−2and5,showing factors and expansion. Separately solve2x²−5x−3=0 by factorisation and substitute each distinct root into the original equation. State the zero-product condition.
sections.exemplar: (x+2)(x−5)=0 givesx²−3x−10=0. The separate equation factors(2x+1)(x−3)=0,sox=−1/2or3. Checks:2(1/4)+5/2−3=0 and18−15−3=0. At least one factor is0 because the product equals0;this rule does not apply by simply setting factors to0 when their product is a nonzero number.

sections.title: 4. Interpret and explore a paper model
sections.prompt: For the CQE14 area28cm² model,form a zero-form equation,solve by factorisation and select feasible dimensions. Give the rejected-root reason and a unit-bearing area check. Explore changing only the area to40cm²:state the changed equation and find/check a positive width and length. Explain what the comparison reveals about using a quadratic model,under the stated exact-rectangle assumption. No peer consultation or invented external research.
sections.exemplar: x(x+3)=28 givesx²+3x−28=(x+7)(x−4)=0. Algebraic roots−7,4;choosewidth4cm,length7cm since dimensions are positive;check4×7=28cm². Changed equationx²+3x−40=0=(x+8)(x−5),sochoose5cmby8cm,check40cm²;−8 is infeasible. The constant changes with the area while the side relation remains fixed. A quadratic model generates candidate dimensions,but units,assumptions and positive-domain checks determine which describe the paper plan.
